Follow-up to #51. A pi extension package such as [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit) can give pi's coding agent more than tools: **prompt templates** (`pi.prompts`), **which tools the model sees** (pit hides the built-in coding tools and shows only `typescript`), and **overrides** of tools and prompt text. This issue describes what pi-action does with each of these now, and how to support them.

Examples use a made-up repository `acme/xyz` with:

```yaml
extensions: |
  github:cv/pit#v0.35.1
```

## What pi-action does now

| Feature | In pi's CLI | In pi-action today |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt templates (`pi.prompts`, `.pi/prompts/*.md`, `~/.pi/agent/prompts`) | `/pit-reflect focus` expands `prompts/pit-reflect.md` (frontmatter `description`, `argument-hint`; body with `$ARGUMENTS`, `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`, `$1`, `${@:2}`) | **Ignored.** `loadExtensions` loads only `pi.durable` (or `pi.extensions`, for providers). `@pi /pit-reflect` goes to the model as plain text |
| Tool exclusion and hiding | pit's `pitLoadout` hides the declarations of `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` and other tools, so the model sees only `typescript` and the `allowedTools` from `pit.json`. The hidden tools can still be called through `tools.*` | **Not possible.** `Thread.open` installs `CodingTools` and then every extension. `root.configure()` gets only `{ model, cwd }`, so the model is always offered `read, write, edit, bash, typescript`. pit's `allowedTools` setting has no effect |
| Overrides of tools and sections | `pi.registerTool` with a built-in name replaces that tool, and `before_agent_start` can change the system prompt | **Partly works, but isn't documented or tested.** pi-durable applies the `wraps` (`wrapTool`, `wrapSection`) of every selected extension, and by default every installed extension is selected, so a pi-durable extension can already wrap `bash` or another extension's section. pi-action doesn't mention this in its docs or test it |

## Proposal

### 1. Tool exclusion and hiding (pi-durable `AgentState`)

pi-durable already has the right controls in `AgentChange` / `AgentState`:

- `tools: { remove: [...] }`: disables a tool completely (the model can't call it, and neither can other tools).
- `modelTools: { remove: [...] }`: the model isn't offered the tool, but other tools can still call it. This matches pit's "hidden but callable".

Add two inputs, which are applied with `root.configure()` on every run (each run reconfigures already, because the model can differ from the last run):

```yaml
exclude_tools: ''        # e.g. "bash": removed completely
model_tools_hidden: ''   # e.g. "read, write, edit, bash": hidden from the model, callable via pit's tools.*
```

- Accept `*` globs, as pit's `allowedTools` does (`compileToolPatterns`).
- Resolve names against the registry after the extensions are installed. If a name matches no tool, write a warning. If the resolved set would leave the model with **no** tools, fail the run.
- When an input is empty, pass `null` so a setting from an earlier run is cleared (the thread stores the agent state).
- Log the tools the model gets in the `🤖` setup line, which today lists each extension's own tools.

**Defaults that extensions declare.** A pi-durable `Extension` can't set `modelTools` itself, but it can do the same thing with a wrap: `wrapTool("read", (t) => ({ ...t, callers: ["tools"] }))` keeps `read` callable from other tools and stops offering it to the model. pit's durable entry could do this for `read`, `write`, `edit` and `bash`, using the `allowedTools` it already reads from `pit.json`. That change belongs in pit, not here. pi-action only needs to (a) document it, and (b) have the inputs above take precedence. Because `modelTools` only narrows and never widens, an input can't bring back a tool that a wrap set to `callers: ["tools"]`. Document this, or add a `model_tools_shown` input that does the reverse with a wrap installed last by pi-action.

### 2. Prompt templates

Load templates from:

1. The `pi.prompts` directories (or files) of every package in `extensions`, including packages that pi-action loads only for `pi.durable`. This is a change to `loadPackage` in `src/extensions.ts`.
2. `xyz/.pi/prompts/*.md`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Anyone who can push a branch can change these files, and a template becomes the user's request.
3. `<agent_dir>/prompts/*.md`, when `agent_dir` is set.

When names collide, the first one in that order wins and the others get a log warning.

Expansion: when the **task** (the text after `@pi`) starts with `/<name>` and a template has that name, pi-action replaces the task with the expanded body. The rules follow pi's: remove the frontmatter, then substitute `$ARGUMENTS`/`$@`, `$1`…`$9`, `${@:N}` and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`. This applies to the `## Task` of the first message, to `{{task}}` in `prompt_template`, to follow-ups (`**@alice** commented …:` followed by the expanded text), and to the `prompt` input for `pr_number` and direct runs. An unknown `/name` stays as it is.

- Log `▶ Request from @alice: /pit-reflect (prompt template from pit)`, and keep the original comment text in the entry's `data` so the thread shows what was typed.
- Optionally, list the templates (name and `description`) in a section, so the model can tell people what exists. Default off, because it costs tokens on every request.

### 3. Overrides

- Document that `wraps` work, and how they are ordered: `CodingTools` first, then the extensions in input order, and the last wrap wins.
- Add a test in `src/thread.test.ts` / `extensions.test.ts` with a faux extension that wraps `bash` and a pit section.
- Duplicate tool **names** across extensions are a different problem. Today pi-durable's composed map keeps the last one. To match pi's `registerTool` override, make this explicit: log `extension X replaces tool bash from coding-tools`, and don't reject the duplicate the way duplicate extension names are rejected.

## Work items

- [ ] `exclude_tools` and `model_tools_hidden` inputs (`action.yml`, `src/inputs.ts`, `Thread.open` → `root.configure`)
- [ ] Validation, warnings, and the tool list in the setup log
- [ ] Prompt templates: loading (`src/extensions.ts`, a new `src/prompts.ts`), expansion (`src/triggers.ts` / `src/context.ts`), `trust_project` gate
- [ ] Tests for wraps and tool replacement
- [ ] Docs: `docs/extensions.md` (new "Tools the model sees" and "Prompt templates" sections), `docs/prompts.md`, `docs/security.md` (templates from the project)
- [ ] Separate PR in pit: hide the coding tools in `pit/durable` with wraps, following `allowedTools`

Follow-up to #51. Today pi-action **doesn't add `AGENTS.md` to the context**. With no extensions the system prompt is empty, and with pit it has only pit's sections. The model sees `AGENTS.md` only if it decides to `read` it (see [how-it-works.md](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#commit-conventions)). pi's own coding agent puts these files into its system prompt. pi-action should do the same, so that a repository's conventions apply from the first request.

Examples use a made-up repository `acme/xyz`, checked out at `/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz`:

```
xyz/
├── AGENTS.md            # repo-wide conventions
├── packages/api/AGENTS.md
└── CLAUDE.md            # used only where there is no AGENTS.md
```

## Proposal

Add a built-in pi-durable extension, `pi-action-context`, that `Thread.open` installs right after `CodingTools` and before the user's extensions. Its one section is `project_context`.

### Which files

These rules match pi's context-file loading as closely as makes sense on a runner:

1. **Global:** `<agent_dir>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`), only when the `agent_dir` input is set. The default agent directory is a new, empty temporary directory.
2. **Workspace:** each directory from the **workspace root** down to the agent's `cwd` (today that's the root itself): `AGENTS.md`, or else `CLAUDE.md`. Never go above `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so files on the runner outside the checkout can't get into the prompt.
3. Nested files below `cwd` (`packages/api/AGENTS.md`) are **not** loaded up front, as in pi. Optionally, list their paths in one sentence, such as "More AGENTS.md files: packages/api/AGENTS.md; read the one for the directory you work in", so the model knows they exist.

### Format

Like pi's "Project Context" block, as one section:

```
<project_context>
# Project Context

Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

## /home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/AGENTS.md

<file contents>
</project_context>
```

- Put it **before** the extensions' sections (it's installed second), so that pit's guidelines come after the repository's rules. pi-durable keeps sections in install order.
- Size limit: a new input `context_files_max_bytes` (default for example 64 KiB in total). If a file is cut, add a note to the section and write a log warning.

### When it's read

Sections render before **every** model request. If the agent edits `AGENTS.md` during a run, the next request gets an `Updated system prompt section "project_context"` system message, and on many providers the prompt cache becomes invalid. Read the files **once per run**: memoize in the extension, keyed by the run, from `Thread.open`. A later run on the same thread gets the new content as a normal section update.

### Input and compatibility

- A new input `context_files: true | false`. This changes behavior, so either default it to `true` and mention it in the release notes, as a `feat` that most users want, or default it to `false` for one minor release. I suggest `true`: pi users expect it, and the docs already tell people to write their conventions in `AGENTS.md`.
- Existing threads: the section shows up as a positional system update on the next request. No migration is needed.

### Security

`AGENTS.md` comes from the checked-out ref, so on a pull request **its author controls it**, and the system prompt carries more weight than a file the model reads. Options, which need a decision:

- On pull requests from forks (`isForkPullRequest`), read `AGENTS.md` from the **base** branch (`git show <base>:AGENTS.md`), or skip the files and log why.
- Add a note to `docs/security.md` that, for pull requests from the same repository, the branch's `AGENTS.md` is used.
- Apply the same HTML-comment and invisible-character removal that the issue body gets (`src/security.ts`)? Probably not for HTML comments, because they're legitimate in `AGENTS.md`. Removing invisible characters is reasonable.

### Not included (possible follow-ups)

`.pi/SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` (replace or extend the system prompt, as in pi). These would fit the same extension as a second section behind `trust_project`.

## Work items

- [ ] `src/context-files.ts`: discovery (workspace-bounded, `AGENTS.md` before `CLAUDE.md`), reading, size limit, once per run
- [ ] Built-in extension installed in `Thread.open` (`src/thread.ts`), with the name `pi-action-context` reserved in `createDurableExtensions`
- [ ] `context_files` and `context_files_max_bytes` inputs (`action.yml`, `src/inputs.ts`)
- [ ] Fork-PR handling
- [ ] Log line in the setup group: `Context files: AGENTS.md (2.1 KiB)`
- [ ] Tests: discovery order, the workspace boundary, the cut, the section text, and no section update when a file changes during a run
- [ ] Docs: `docs/how-it-works.md` (replace "pi-action does not add them to the prompt"), `docs/prompts.md` (what pi receives), `docs/security.md`, README inputs table

Follow-up to #51. pi-action **doesn't load skills**: no `SKILL.md` discovery, no `<available_skills>` list, no `/skill:name`. In pi's coding agent (and in pit's CLI extension, `formatPitSkillsForPrompt`), the system prompt lists each skill's name, description and location, and the model reads the full `SKILL.md` when a task matches it. pi-action should do the same, so skills shipped in a repository or a package work in CI too.

Examples use a made-up repository `acme/xyz`:

```
xyz/
└── .pi/skills/
    └── release/
        ├── SKILL.md          # ---\nname: release\ndescription: Cut a release of xyz...\n---
        └── scripts/bump.sh
```

and `extensions: github:acme/xyz-skills#v1`, a package with `"pi": { "skills": ["./skills"] }`.

## Proposal

### Discovery

Look in these places, in this order. When names collide, the first one wins and the rest get a log warning:

1. Packages in `extensions` (and a new optional `skills` input with the same spec syntax, for packages that contain only skills): `pi.skills` directories, or else a top-level `skills/` directory, as pi does. For packages, pi-action should **also** install packages that have only skills. Today `loadPackage` warns "has no pi extensions".
2. Project: `xyz/.pi/skills/` and `xyz/.agents/skills/`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Skills can tell the agent to run scripts, and anyone who can push a branch can change them.
3. User: `<agent_dir>/skills/`, when `agent_dir` is set.

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md`, found recursively. Parse the frontmatter following the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) rules, as pi does:

- `name`: required, lowercase `a-z0-9-`, at most 64 characters, and the same as the directory name. A skill that breaks these rules is skipped with a warning.
- `description`: required, at most 1024 characters.
- `disable-model-invocation: true`: not listed for the model, only available as `/skill:name`.

### Prompt section

A built-in pi-durable extension section, `available_skills`. It can share the extension with the `AGENTS.md` work in the sibling issue. It's rendered once per run (memoized), so the prompt cache stays valid:

```
<available_skills>
The following skills provide specialized instructions for specific tasks.
Use the read tool to load a skill's SKILL.md in full when the task matches its description.
Resolve relative paths in a skill against its directory.

  <skill>
    <name>release</name>
    <description>Cut a release of xyz...</description>
    <location>/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/.pi/skills/release/SKILL.md</location>
  </skill>
</available_skills>
```

- Locations are absolute. Package skills live in `$RUNNER_TEMP/pi-action-extensions-*`, which the coding tools can read.
- **pit:** when `typescript` is the only tool the model sees (see the tool-hiding issue), the instruction should say `workspace.read` instead of "the read tool", as pit's own text does. The section can check `input.agent.tools` when it renders, so pit doesn't need a separate skills section.
- Leave the section out when there are no skills.

### Explicit use: `@pi /skill:release 2.4.0`

When the task starts with `/skill:<name>`, pi-action puts the skill's full `SKILL.md` (without the frontmatter, and with a note on its directory) in the message, followed by the arguments. This works for both the first message and follow-ups. It uses the same task-rewriting hook as prompt templates (see the prompts/tools issue). An unknown skill name gets an error reply instead of being sent to the model.

### Logging

In the setup group: `Skills: release (project), changelog (xyz-skills)`, plus a warning for each skipped or shadowed skill.

## Work items

- [ ] `src/skills.ts`: discovery, frontmatter parsing and validation, collisions
- [ ] Install packages that contain only skills; the optional `skills` input (`action.yml`, `src/inputs.ts`)
- [ ] `trust_project` gate for project skills
- [ ] `available_skills` section in the built-in extension; tool-aware wording
- [ ] `/skill:name` expansion
- [ ] Tests: discovery order, validation, the gate, section text, expansion
- [ ] Docs: a new `docs/skills.md`, links from README and `docs/extensions.md`, and `docs/security.md`
